service.description: a program that should be running. It is stored on the same entity its `process` component lands on: the service records what is wanted, the process records what is actually running, and a `stop` component beside it means the program is no longer wanted

command.description: the command line to run, argv joined by spaces — the supervisor's own copy, kept here rather than read back off the running process, because restarting needs the command that was asked for and not what the kernel reports

cwd.description: the working directory to run it in; absent means the supervisor's own working directory

restart.description: what to do when it exits, using systemd's three values; absent means never, so a service that does not set it runs once and stays down

attempts.description: how many times the supervisor has restarted it after an exit — the backoff grows with this number, and a run that outlives the longest backoff resets the count

process.description: a program running on this machine, tracked by pid — whether or not this package started it

pid.description: the process id on the machine tracking it — the only durable handle an adopted process has

command.description: the command line it was launched with, argv joined by spaces; absent when the process was adopted rather than started here

cwd.description: the working directory it was launched in; absent for the same reason as command

exit.description: the process has ended — never rewritten, and deleted only by the transaction that records the next attempt on a supervised entity

code.description: the exit code it reported; absent when the end of the process was observed but the code was not (a signal killed the wrapper, or nothing was watching)
